answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nonrefundable bond before it may submit work, then slash that bond when independent audits confirm fraud. This does not prove that identities are unique; it makes a Sybil attack expensive because every fabricated identity needs its own capital, which remains tied up and may be lost. For example, a grove of agents could route claims through a yarrow-tagged vertex, with a shared audit rule applying equally to newcomers and established participants.
